connections.observation: s002 traces μορφή from multiplicity to singularity; s003 traces ἰδέα from the different forms god might appear in to his own single ἰδέα from which he might depart. Held together, the two terms make visible a movement from questioned plurality (ἄλλοτε ἐν ἄλλαις ἰδέαις, εἰς πολλὰς μορφάς) to denied plurality (πολλὰς μορφάς) to affirmed permanence in one form (ἐν τῇ αὑτοῦ μορφῇ). The lexical doubling enacts the argument's contraction from many to one.

s001 shows ἀλλοιόω applied serially to bodies, plants, soul, artifacts, and god; s009 shows ἥκιστα repeated through the same sequence. The conjunction makes visible the argumentative ladder: each rung states that what is best-conditioned is ἥκιστα ἀλλοιοῦται, and each rung's subject rises in ontological station until reaching god, who is ἥκιστα altered because πάντῃ ἄριστα ἔχει.

s006 records ἁπλοῦς at the section's opening question, middle conclusion, and final summary; s007 records γόης/γοητεύω at the same three positions. The paired recurrence makes visible that simplicity and the denial of sorcery frame and close the same arc: whether god is ἁπλοῦν or γόητα is the opening alternative; that he μένει ἁπλῶς and is not a γόης is the conclusion.

s004 accumulates seven instances of ψεῦδος; s005 distinguishes ὡς ἀληθῶς ψεῦδος from its μίμημα and εἴδωλον, which is οὐ πάνυ ἄκρατον. Together they make visible that the dense repetition of ψεῦδος is not mere accumulation but a doubled structure: the term recurs across two ontological levels, one located ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ and hated πάντες, the other ἐν τοῖς λόγοις and conditionally useful.

s012 shows the pairing λόγος/ἔργον recur three times in the argument about falsehood and truth; s006 shows ἁπλοῦς recur three times in the argument about divine form. The conjunction makes visible a structural parallelism: the section moves twice through the same rhythm—question, reasoning, summary—first about divine constancy in form, then about divine truthfulness in word and deed.

s015 notes that ἀψευδές appears first as the concluded divine attribute, then immediately in Thetis's tragic speech; s016 notes the fourfold αὐτός anaphora accumulating Apollo's actions. Held together, they make visible that the term ἀψευδές, just affirmed as divine, is placed in the mouth of one who trusted that attribute and was betrayed—and the repetition of αὐτός concentrates the identity of singer, speaker, and killer in the god himself.

s014 traces the ψευδ- family saturating the section's second half, culminating in ἀψευδές; s015 shows ἀψευδές occur twice in immediate succession. Together they make visible that the argument's terminological density reaches its peak in the word ἀψευδές, which is then immediately tested by its placement in Thetis's mouth—affirmed, then cited in a context of divine deception.

s011 contrasts βέλτιον/κάλλιον with χεῖρον/αἴσχιον as directions of divine change; s021 shows ἑκών recur first in the denial that anyone willingly makes himself worse, then in the denial that anyone willingly accepts falsehood. The conjunction makes visible that the argument proceeds by the same structure in both parts: no one ἑκών moves toward the worse, whether in ontological change (381c) or epistemic deception (382a).

s010 catalogues bodies, plants, soul, and crafted objects with their affecting agents (food, winds, external πάθος, time); s001 shows ἀλλοιόω applied to the same sequence. Together they make visible that the argument ascends through ontological levels by concrete analogy: each entity's resistance to ἀλλοίωσις is tested against particular material causes before the principle is applied to god, who faces no such external agents.

s017 notes that falsehood in words is called a φάρμακον useful for defense; s005 distinguishes such falsehood as μίμημα and εἴδωλον, explicitly not ἄκρατον ψεῦδος. Held together, they make visible that the ontological demotion of verbal falsehood to a copy enables its practical promotion to a remedy: because it is an εἴδωλον of soul-falsehood rather than the thing itself, it can serve human need.

s013 traces the φαντάζω family (φαντάζεσθαι, φάντασμα, φαντασίας) from the opening question through the lying question to the final denial; s007 traces γόης/γοητεύω through the same three positions. The conjunction makes visible a lexical alliance: appearing falsely (φαντάζω) and performing sorcery (γοητεύω) track together across the section's structure, both denied of god in the final summary.

s008 shows μεταβάλλω recur at the question of self-change, the principle of minimal change, the direction of change, and the final rule; s002 shows μορφή move from many forms to one form. Together they make visible that μεταβολή is the verb answered by μορφή as its substantive result: the question of divine μεταβάλλειν resolves into remaining ἐν τῇ αὑτοῦ μορφῇ.

s020 clusters παντοῖος and παντοδαπός around the denied divine multiplicity in poetry and mothers' tales; s002 shows μορφή contract from πολλὰς μορφάς to τῇ αὑτοῦ μορφῇ. The conjunction makes visible that the rejected poetic images (gods in all-varied forms) are answered by the philosophical conclusion (god in his one form): the παντο- vocabulary is denied in the same movement that affirms singularity.

s018 shows τύπος appear as δεύτερον τύπον and then τοὺς τύπους τούτους; s019 shows Adeimantus accept these as νόμοις. The conjunction makes visible that the section concludes by recharacterizing its own speech: what Socrates offers as a τύπος (pattern, outline, model for theological speech) Adeimantus receives as something he would use ὡς νόμοις—the formulation crosses from description to legislation.

s023 traces the closing sequence from denying chorus to barring teachers to the guardians becoming θεοσεβεῖς τε καὶ θεῖοι; s019 notes the final word νόμοις. Together they make visible that the argument's endpoint is simultaneously theological (the guardians to become θεῖοι) and legislative (the τύποι to function as νόμοι): the section moves from theoretical rules about divine nature to their institutional enforcement for the guardians' formation.

s022 notes κυριώτατος appear twice, localizing falsehood in the most authoritative part of oneself and about the most authoritative matters; s005 identifies this as ἡ ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ ἄγνοια, contrasted with verbal falsehood. The conjunction makes visible that the ontological distinction between soul-falsehood and word-falsehood is simultaneously a hierarchical distinction: what is κυριώτατον is the soul concerning τὰ ὄντα, and falsehood there is ὡς ἀληθῶς ψεῦδος, while words carry only its εἴδωλον.

s004 accumulates ψεῦδος seven times in close density; s017 notes that verbal falsehood is called a φάρμακον. The conjunction makes visible a movement within the repetition: ψεῦδος is first divided (soul vs. words), then the verbal form is qualified (μίμημα, εἴδωλον, not ἄκρατον), and finally repositioned (φάρμακον, χρήσιμον against enemies and the deranged). The term's density enacts its own examination and conditional rehabilitation.

s016 shows the fourfold αὐτός anaphora in the Aeschylus fragment accumulating Apollo as singer, guest, speaker, and killer; s006 shows the section culminate in θεὸς ἁπλοῦν καὶ ἀληθές. Held together, they make visible a collision: the philosophical conclusion that god is ἁπλοῦν (simple, without duplicity) is immediately followed by a poetic voice insisting on the god's sustained presence through contradictory actions (αὐτός blessing, αὐτός slaying). The tragic anaphora enacts the multiplicity the argument denies.

elements.context: ἀνάγκη (380e); πῶς δʼ οὔ; / ναί / ἀνάγκη, ἔφη (381a); ἅπασα, ἔφη, ἀνάγκη ἔμοιγε δοκεῖ (381c)

new_signals.observation: ἀνάγκη punctuates the argument's ascent from bodies to god: once as the necessity that what departs its ἰδέα is moved by self or other, again (implicitly through assenting πῶς δʼ οὔ, ναί) that the best-conditioned is least altered, and finally as ἅπασα ἀνάγκη affirming that god remains unchanging. The term marks the binding force of each argumentative step.

Forms of ἀληθής appear four times in the second half: twice qualifying ψεῦδος (the truly-real falsehood in the soul), once as the standard to which myth-making assimilates falsehood, and finally as the attribute paired with ἁπλοῦν in the conclusion about god. The family moves from framing falsehood to naming divine truth.

elements.context: πάντων ἥκιστα τῆς ἑαυτοῦ ἰδέας ἐκβαίνειν
εἴπερ τι ἐξίσταιτο τῆς αὑτοῦ ἰδέας

new_signals.observation: Two verbs of departure from one's ἰδέα occur in immediate succession at 380d: ἐκβαίνειν (stepping out) and ἐξίστημι (standing out, being displaced). The doubling intensifies the spatial grammar of constancy: remaining or departing from one's form.

elements.context: τὸ ὑγιέστατον καὶ ἰσχυρότατον ἥκιστα ἀλλοιοῦται
τὴν ἀνδρειοτάτην καὶ φρονιμωτάτην ἥκιστʼ ἄν τι ἔξωθεν πάθος ταράξειεν

new_signals.observation: Three paired superlatives mark the ascending analogies: body (healthiest and strongest), soul (most courageous and most thoughtful), god (most beautiful and best). The grammatical parallelism enacts the structural parallelism of the argument through entities of increasing ontological rank.

elements.context: μηδʼ αὖ ὑπὸ τούτων ἀναπειθόμεναι αἱ μητέρες τὰ παιδία ἐκδειματούντων

new_signals.observation: Mothers appear as those who, persuaded by false myths, frighten children with tales of gods wandering at night in many forms. The figure localizes the transmission of theological error in domestic pedagogy, distinct from the poetic and institutional contexts elsewhere in the section.

elements.form: θεοὺς βλασφημῶσιν ... τοὺς παῖδας ἀπεργάζωνται δειλοτέρους
elements.context: ἵνα μὴ ἅμα μὲν εἰς θεοὺς βλασφημῶσιν, ἅμα δὲ τοὺς παῖδας ἀπεργάζωνται δειλοτέρους

new_signals.observation: The mothers' false tales produce two simultaneous harms, marked by ἅμα μέν ... ἅμα δέ: blasphemy against gods and the production of more cowardly children. The pairing connects theological error directly to the corruption of courage in the young.
